subject: Marketplace private offer: rollforward, credits, and PO timing
messages:
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: natalie.huang@amazon.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com; sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-10T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Marketplace private offer: rolling forward term and applied credit options

Natalie —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. We're preparing the private offer paperwork for Acme Analytics (deal RDW-PO-98761). Two asks so we can move to signature this week: 

1) Can the current private offer be rolled forward to a 12-month annualized term instead of the current 6-month term without triggering pricing re-approval? Acme wants predictable month-to-month per-token rates for budgeting.

2) Acme negotiated a one-time onboarding credit (USD 75k) tied to year-1 usage. We need guidance on how that credit should be represented on the AWS private offer (credit line vs. rebate on the initial invoice). Marissa from finance is CC'd and will confirm invoicing impact.

I'm attaching a draft PO and the AWS template for reference. Proposed next steps: you update the private offer language indicating term=12 months, add a line for the onboarding credit, and we route to Acme procurement for signature. Can you confirm timing?

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Attachments: PO_Draft_Acme_2026.pdf, aws_private_offer_template.docx
From: natalie.huang@amazon.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: rolling forward term and applied credit options

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. Quick answers: 

1) Rolling to a 12-month term is feasible but requires a quick internal approval depending on the visibility band of the SKU. I can start the change; will flag treasury if we need pricing re-approval. Expect a 24–48h turnaround.

2) On credits: AWS prefers credits show as a separate line item on the private offer that reduces the net payable. We can either set it as a prepaid credit balance or implement a one-time invoice credit. If Acme wants the credit to appear on their invoice schedule, invoice-credit is simplest. Please confirm which option Acme prefers and whether the credit should amortize across months or be applied to the first invoice.

I'll draft the amended private offer and return it as a .docx for RDW review.

—Natalie
Marketplace Partner Manager, AWS Marketplace
Natalie.Huang@amazon.com
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: natalie.huang@amazon.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com; sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-11T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: rolling forward term and applied credit options

Natalie —

Great, thanks. Acme's procurement (Timothy) wants the credit to show on the invoice schedule and apply to the first two monthly invoices (50/50 split). They also prefer the credit to be explicit on the private offer so it's visible to their finance team.

Marissa — can you confirm whether Redwood will recognize the onboarding credit as a contra-revenue line or apply it as an upfront bill credit? Our accounting prefers recognizing as contra-revenue spread across the 12-month period, but we can adapt if Acme's auditors require a different flow.

I'll loop Timothy in the next message to capture official procurement language.

Thanks,
Rafael
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com; natalie.huang@amazon.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: rolling forward term and applied credit options

Rafael / Natalie —

Accounting here. Redwood prefers to recognize the onboarding credit as contra-revenue amortized over the contract term (12 months). Operationally that's cleaner for ASC and internal reporting. We'll generate an invoice schedule that lists the gross charges per month, then the monthly amortized credit (-6,250 USD/month) so net amounts match the agreed total.

If Acme's procurement/legal requires the credit be shown as a prepaid credit on AWS's side, we can include language in the private offer that the credit is applied to the first two invoices (50/50) for cash-flow purposes; our bookkeeping will still amortize for revenue recognition. Please add a short clause: 

"Onboarding credit of USD 75,000 to be applied 50% to Invoice 1 and 50% to Invoice 2; Redwood will amortize the credit over the 12-month contract term for revenue recognition."

Attach instructions: I've uploaded a simple invoice schedule spreadsheet to the attachments.

-Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Timothy Cole <timothy.cole@acmeanalytics.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.com; natalie.huang@amazon.com
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com; marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-13T10:09:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: rolling forward term and applied credit options

Rafael / Natalie / Marissa —

Confirming Acme's preference: apply the USD 75,000 onboarding credit 50/50 to the first two invoices. We need the private offer to include the credit clause exactly as Marissa suggested, and a line in the PO called "Onboarding credit (one-time) — USD 75,000". Also, please ensure the PO includes the renewal window and cancellation notice (30 days).

One logistic ask: can Redwood and AWS keep the DocuSign flow simple — procurement signs, then AWS counter-signs, then Redwood executes? If there's an AWS-side automated acceptance that replaces signature, flag that now so we can get legal comfortable.

Thanks,
Tim Cole
Head of Cloud Procurement | Acme Analytics
From: rafael.mendes@redwood.com
To: natalie.huang@amazon.com; timothy.cole@acmeanalytics.com; procurement@acmeanalytics.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com; sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-14T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer: rolling forward term and applied credit options

Team —

Thanks for the confirmations. Natalie — if you can return a draft private offer by EOD tomorrow with the term set to 12 months, the onboarding credit line as discussed, and a 30-day cancellation clause, we will route to Acme's DocuSign. I've attached the PO draft and the invoice schedule for your reference.

For clarity on the signature flow: Acme procurement (Tim) signs first via DocuSign PowerForm, AWS will countersign (Natalie, let us know if this is automated or manual), then Redwood will complete execution. After countersignature we'll provision the dedicated SKU and update the billing schedule in our system.

If we get the amended offer back by EOD tomorrow we can hit signature before EOD Monday and align provisioning for 8/22.

Appreciate everyone's help —
Rafael Mendes
